The DG type considered in this study is Typel DG which injects real as well as reactive power to the system. The objective of this study is minimization of total generation cost with maximizing the DG owner profit. This paper also presents that the payment by the loads get reduced by placement of DG. The study is conducted on IEEE WSCC 9 bus system.

articleTitle: Short Circuit Studies on a Distribution System Integrated with Various Distributed Generations
abstract: Distributed Generations (DGs) are one of the important and prominent smart grid technologies that will lead the world to meet the objective of sustainable energy for the future. There are many technical as well as social benefits that can be achieved using DGs but at the same time DGs also offer a set of challenges which need to be addressed aswell. This paper will present the issues related to the fault level contributions in a Distribution System (DS) with and without DGs. The cases considered for the study are by analyzing the fault levels with different kind of DGs (Diesel, PV system and Wind DFIG) integrated with the DS. The effect of grounding during an asymmetrical fault considering various transformer winding configurations is presented in this paper. A comparative study has been made from the considered cases and conclusions are drawn. MiPower, a Power System software simulation tool has been used for carrying out the Short circuit studies.

articleTitle: Protection Coordination in Grid Connected and Islanded Mode of Microgrid
abstract: Protection of modern power system is facing new challenges due to presence of distributed generation (DG). Any microgrid can operate in grid connected and islanded mode. Since short circuit level in both cases is different, separate protection scheme is required. In this paper, settings of numerical directional overcurrent relay are obtained separately for both modes. This is achieved by formulating a nonlinear optimization problem which is solved using three techniques. Further the scheme for online update of settings based on operating mode is also proposed. Primary and backup relays are coordinated using the optimal settings which confirm reliable protection of a grid under both topologies. MATLAB/SIMULINK platform is used for 9 bus test system designing and coding.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Four-Leg Four-Wire Topology in High Power Factor Converter addressing the problem of unbalanced source currents
abstract: Unbalanced voltage supplies, load and nonlinear loads leads to poor Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), generates reactive power and excess neutral current leads to degradation of power quality. To mitigate these issues three phase three leg four wire (3P3L4W) topology with Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) based Zero Current Injection (ZCI) algorithm is implemented to balance the dc link capacitor voltage, improve THD and reduce unbalanced supply voltage condition. But source currents are not sinusoidal to overcome this limitation a three phase four-leg four wire (3P4L4W) diode clamped converter (DCC) is proposed, which is discussed in detail in this paper with simulation results using MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement in SyRG-PV-BES Based Standalone Microgrid Using SOGI-WIF Control Algorithm
abstract: A three-phase four-wire solar photovoltaic (PV) with a battery energy storage (BES) and a pico-hydro turbine driven synchronous reluctance generator (SyRG) based microgrid is proposed in this paper. Where, a boost converter serves the function of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of a PV array. Moreover, a BES is incorporated in the system to provide required management of active power within the system. In comparison to a conventional control algorithm of a voltage source converter (VSC), the proposed control algorithm provides extra function of compensation of reactive power, harmonics mitigation and elimination of neutral current. The proposed SOGIFLL-WIF (Second Order Generalized Integrator with Frequency Locked Loop with Inner Loop Filter) control algorithm has an extra feed-forward loop, which provides DC offset removal, higher order harmonics mitigation, simple structure, fast convergence and moreover good dynamic and steady state response. An experimental prototype of the system is developed and tested under different situations such as load unbalancing and solar insolation changes to confirm the effectiveness and viabilty of control strategy.

articleTitle: SVM Tuned NARX Method for Wind speed & power Prediction in Electricity Generation
abstract: Due to continuous depleting of conventional energy reserves as well as global warming issues has diverted world attention towards non conventional energy sources. Out of different non conventional energy sources wind can be consider the cleanest source with minimum possible pollution or harmful emissions and has the potential to decrease the relying on conventional energy sources. Wind energy can play a major role to meet our energy demands, however, it faces various problems such as intermittent nature, instability in frequency. To reduce such issues the idea of futuristic wind speed trends and weather conditions are required. This paper suggests a method for wind speed, power forecasting using NARX and Support Vector Machine (SVM). This hybrid technique can select most suitable data segment from available data. These data segments are used for the training and validation of SVM model. The historical data used is from Kolkata region wind energy farm.

articleTitle: Transmission congestion management with FACTS devices using BBO Algorithm
abstract: this paper presents Biogeography-based optimization (BBO) techniques for the excellent location to achieve minimum transmission active power loss, optimal cost, and optimal bus voltage. The proposed methods are authentic in the IEEE-30 bus system with power flow equation using a Newton-Raphson algorithm. The execution of IEEE-30 bus system is computed on different reactive loading condition. Here we are present the BBO and PSO's comparative result using distinct optimization techniques. In the end, BBO is best for the transmission of active power loss minimization and total cost of the system at the various loading for the IEEE-30 bus system as compared to PSO (Particle Swarm optimization). Biogeography-base optimization is the best solution, is to reduce active power loss, system operating cost including the cost of FACTS devices and congestion in the transmission network.

articleTitle: Analysis of distribution tariff structures in the presence of non-linear load
abstract: In restructured power systems, distribution pricing has emerged as a vital driver to ensure economic efficiency of network operations. An increasing emphasis is being laid on the design of cost-reflective tariff structures so as to send appropriate economic signals to electricity consumers. Furthermore, with changing load profile and injection of large harmonic currents by the consumers in present distribution systems, designing an efficient tariff structure is a challenging task This paper investigates two most widely used tariff structures, viz. two-part and three-part, in the presence of non-linear load. Demand power and energy are calculated with varying percentage of non-linear load in the distribution system, and annual distribution price for both tariff structures is compared. Test results obtained for IEEE -18 bus radial distribution system indicate that three-part distribution tariff structure is significantly cost-reflective as compared to the two-part structure.

articleTitle: Power flow management for grid stability using TCSC device
abstract: Flexible AC Transmission System (FACTS) devices are used to reduce the stress on a transmission lines. This stress is due to the heavily loaded system which affects the system operation and stability. In this paper, a FACTS device-Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC) device is used to compensate the reactance of the transmission line which enhances the power flow. The objective is to reduce the losses as well as minimize the generation cost. Different cases are studied for optimal placement of TCSC device in the transmission line. The whole work is carried on IEEE 14 bus system. Mipower software has been used to obtain the load flow analysis by using Newton-Raphson method.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Low Cost Acoustic Chamber for Electric Machines
abstract: This paper discusses the design and performance analysis of low-cost acoustic chamber for measurement of acoustic noise and vibration of electric machines. The purpose of this paper is to find the parameters that allow the characterization of acoustic chamber thereby making an attempt in deriving and obtaining the data of acoustic chamber. The parameters that are being calculated are acoustic transfer function, reverberation time, sound power level and cut-off frequency of acoustic chamber. To obtain the transfer function of acoustic chamber, a pair of microphones and amplifier as a source of sound have been used. Based on the results of transfer functions obtained between the pair of microphones, the cut-off frequency of acoustic chamber is determined and validated through Inverse Square Law. Noise measurements are conducted in both an ordinary environment (laboratory) and acoustic chamber. The acoustic chamber provides the free-field conditions, which satisfy the standard parameters required for the design and test for acoustic chamber. The results obtained both in an ordinary environment and acoustic chamber are compared to produce useful practical information about the noise level change caused by sound fields. The results obtained are found to be helpful in understanding the physical features and characteristics of acoustic chamber.

articleTitle: Application of Renewable Energy Sources as Compensator in Power system
abstract: The power generation from renewable energy sources has become attractive to meet the increasing energy demand over the globe. The grid integration of renewable energy farms is gaining popularity nowadays. The residual inverter capacity of these farms can be utilized to perform some additional tasks along with their basic operation of inversion. In this paper, the residual capacity of grid side inverters of large-scale solar and wind power farms is utilized as a static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) and a static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) devices in order to improve the overall power system performance such as to regulate line voltages, providing reactive power compensation and to increase the grid power transfer limit. The proposed control is verified in the MATLAB / Simulink environment.

articleTitle: A new Three Phase 5L-UIPFC with reduced part count for High Speed Gen-Set Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel 3-Ø five-level unidirectional improved power factor converter (3P5LUIPFC) with reduced device count for high speed generator set applications is proposed. The proposed topology as similar to multi stacked conventional multilevel topologies, however, additional clamping devices to attain intermediate dc link voltages are not required. In addition, there is only one physical bi directional controlled switch is required for attaining zero voltage level. The overall topology structure offers not only minimum devices count and also standing voltage stress across devices are minimum. This can improves the efficacy of the converter system. Level shifting sine pulse width modulation technique is implemented to generate desired PWM signals. MATLAB Simulation and prototype experimentation is carried out to verify the performance of proposed topology under given operating conditions.

articleTitle: A New Transmission Line Differential Protection based on Fault current DC Transients
abstract: This paper presents a new transmission line differential protection using fault current DC transients. The behaviour of fault current DC transients for different types of faults are analysed for proposing a new differential protection criteria. The proposed method clearly distinguishes internal and external faults which aids in improving the sensitivity and security of the transmission system. Different types of the fault like solid ground fault, high resistance faults, outfeed effect are considered and compared with the conventional differential protection. For analysing the proposed method a 10 bus system is considered and simulated using PSCAD software. From the results it is observed that the proposed differential protection operates well for different types of network configurations and for various types of faults at a faster fault identification rate.

articleTitle: Abridged Methodology Development for Analyzing Transformer Winding During Lightning Surges
abstract: Instances of lightning impulse pose a severe threat to transformer winding. A steep wavefront frequency of as great as tens of thousands of times, compared to peak rate of normal power frequency creates intense and rapid change of electric field in the transformer winding. This rapid change is constituted significantly in some part of winding, leading to excessive stress on insulation present in that part of winding. Researchers have used terminal measurements performed on transformer winding, to estimate the severity of lightning impulses. The detailed model has also been proposed in literature to understand the in-depth voltage distribution across the winding height. The time taken to develop such detailed model is high and resource intensive. This paper deals with proposition of methodology which requires minimal resources and takes comparatively less time to analyze impulse voltage distribution across winding turns, accurately.

articleTitle: Protocol for Smart grid for two-way communication
abstract: A Protocol for smart grid has been created for managing demand and supply as per customer needs and use of renewable energy. Markov process and Poisson's method are used for two-way communication and calculating average cost of energy production at main grid. The electricity generation at consumer end from renewable sources, is stored in batteries and used when required and send back to main grid if excess. The average cost of power production is calculated, and appropriate action is suggested to increase the efficiency of the entire system.

articleTitle: Identification of Three Zones of Mal-Operations in Series Capacitor Compensated Transmission Network
abstract: This work investigates the problems faced by conventional distance relays present on the Series Capacitor (SC) with 40% compensation at the midpoint of transmission network. The detail examinations of mal-operations in three-zones of distance relay on series capacitor compensated line are studied in this work. Finally, the impacts of SC on adjacent line relays are observed. The accurate apparent impedance is estimated based on DFT-mimic filter algorithm. The test power system and simulations are developed in MATLAB/Simulink Software.

articleTitle: Detection of Open Circuiting of Secondary Winding of Current Transformer Using Combined Feature of Hilbert Transform and Stockwell Transform
abstract: This paper presents a technique based on combined application of the Hilbert Transform and Stockwell Transform for the detection of open circuiting of secondary winding of the current transformer. The proposed algorithm has been tested in the presence of the resistive inductive as well as capacitive loads. The proposed study is performed in MATLAB/Simulink environment. The simulation results show effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for detection of open circuiting of the secondary winding of the current transformer core.

articleTitle: Investigation of Water Drop on Silicone Rubber Insulator for High Voltage Transmission Line Using FEM
abstract: The water drop on the silicone rubber insulator surface during contaminated conditions under various changing parameters has already been investigated. In general, there is a lack of investigation of electrostatic parameters during dry and humid air conditions. This study shows the simulation of the water drop at the 90-degree contact angle on clean silicon rubber insulator under high voltage stress in 2D space dimension is shown, by using the finite element method based software. This software is used for numerical calculation of potential, normalized electric field and polarization density distribution. These field distribution is used to visualize and analyze above electrostatic parameters for comparison, under dry and humid air conditions. Furthermore, the simulation results show that potential distribution is not much affected during both dry and humid air conditions where the electric field is higher in case of humid air condition compared to dry air at triple point junction. Results also show that the field enhancement ratio in humid air condition is two times, wherein the dry air it is less. In addition, Polarization density at the triple point in humid air is increased more in comparison to dry air conditions. This paperwork can be used to learn about the initial behaviour of the water drop on clean silicone rubber insulator surface under both the dry and humid air boundary conditions using the finite element method.

articleTitle: Control of Fifth-order Buck-Boost Converter
abstract: A fifth-order buck-boost converter suitable for feeding point of load applications is presented in this paper. It offers finely tuned buck-boost conversion together with less ripple content in the source current thereby reducing the filtering requirements at the source side. The salient feature of this proposed converter is that it offers more duty ratio range for bucking operation. Mathematical analysis is presented to predetermine the salient features of the proposed converter. Voltage transformation ratio is formulated for CCM operation and the relevant equations defining the L and C components are evolved. A set of small-signal transfer functions are obtained and used in the controller design. A 50Watt, 100 kHz prototype of fifth-order buck-boost converter is built for experiment. The adopted load voltage is either 48 or 15 V. A 36V dc-source is used for powering the prototype converter operation both in simulation and experimentation. The effectiveness of the proposed converter is verified.

articleTitle: Design of Encoder Simulator to Augment Data Acquisition for 4 – Dimensional Rotary Table in Thermal Vacuum Chamber
abstract: Incremental optical encoder, responsible for tracking stepper motor's rotational increment, is widely used in 4 -dimensional rotary tables of thermal vacuum chambers. This paper aims at development of a program using KEIL software making rotational measurement unforced. The main objective includes incorporating flexibilities of easy handling, managing and storing of different combinations of inputs for simulating the package. The requirement for minimal hardware is satisfied by implementation of microcontroller, AT89852. Inclusion of LCD and Push Button matrix interfacing in the formulation of program assists in reduction of procedural steps allowing better simulation of the system. The program developed for encoder simulator supports testing and verification of encoder reader's event detection capabilities required for precise rotary table's position calculation it finds application in monitoring speed of motors by controlling frequency, electric drives, 4- dimensional motion of cameras in space and send letter in messages.

articleTitle: Flexibility in Indian Grid Operation with High Penetration of Grid-Connected Renewable Energy
abstract: This paper describes about the requirement vis-à-vis possible achievability of flexibility in the Indian grid operation in general with the massive development of variable renewable energy sources and consequent high level of penetration of the same into the grid. Indian experience in this context with problems faced with the addition of such type of generation into the system, the measures taken to cope up with the situation and possible course of action contemplated for the future have been vividly described.

articleTitle: Microgrid Economic load Dispatch including Storage and Reserve
abstract: In microgrid systems, economic load dispatch (ELD) with dynamic approach is preferred over static approach because it not only minimizes the cost but also helps to coordinate between distribution generators (DGs). In this paper, microgrid system consisting of diesel engines (DE), wind turbine (WT), a fuel cell (FC) and a battery, model has been developed and analyzed with considering the effect of reserve, emissions, fluctuations in renewable power and the price variation of the grid. The main objective is to minimize the operation and pollutant treatment cost. Microgrid system analysis is done for two operating modes that is the grid connected and the island mode under four different scheduling schemes. By using the GAMS software with MATLAB interfacing, power and cost analysis of each scheduling scheme is done in detail. In the grid connected mode, priority is given either to the DGs or the main grid to have power exchange between the grid and the microgrid. In islanded mode, battery is used instead of the grid for the economic load dispatch.

articleTitle: Locating Source of Oscillation using Mode Shape and Oscillating Energy Flow Techniques
abstract: In this paper, two different techniques of locating the source of oscillation source are compared viz. Mode shape method and Oscillating energy flow method. Mode shape for each generator is calculated using the measurement signal, generator speed. The mode shapes are calculated corresponding to inter-area mode which is filtered out using wavelet synchro squeezing technique. The generator which has a leading phase angle for that mode is said to be responsible for creating disturbance in the system. Also, oscillating energy flow using measurements at generator buses are calculated for each generator. The oscillating energy flow technique is related to damping provided by the generator in the system. The generator which has negative damping is considered to be the source of oscillation in the system. Mode shape technique is a time window based technique and gives a more correct result for the large time window. However, the oscillating energy flow method can be calculated at each time instants. Another challenge with mode shape technique in locating the source of disturbance is to comment on damping contribution from a generator if a particular generator is not participating in that mode. Measurements from two different systems Kundur system and New England system are used to identify the source of oscillation in the system.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Standalone PV System at Varying Loads
abstract: Employing solar power system is a good viable option to establish a stand against fossil fuel dependence and high percentage of carbon dioxide emitted by industrialized world. A complete model of standalone PV System is presented in this paper. Matlab/Simulink is used for the implementation of mathematical models of the system. The system is analyzed under different temperatures and varying load conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of PV Trackers for Remote Rural Electrification
abstract: Access to electricity in remote rural areas has now become imperative as this will lead to the overall development of the agrarian population. The most convenient means to electrify the villages in these areas is to use Solar PV systems. This renewable energy technology being available only in daytime needs to be highly efficient so that besides just meeting the required load during sunshine hours, adequate electricity can be stored in the batteries to be used during night time. Such requirement can be easily met by the use of Solar PV trackers-single axis and dual axis. This study aims to compare the performance of three different mounting arrangements for PV system-fixed mounting, single axis trackers and dual axis trackers installed in remote rural areas of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan. The performance analysis is based on the comparison of technical and economic metrics. It is observed that the technical performance of dual axis trackers is the best in regard to the PV capacity requirement which is 11% less, the total energy production which is 15% more and the capacity utilization which is 6.9% more in comparison to the fixed mounting arrangement. But from economic point of view, the dual axis trackers are the most expensive with net present cost of 2.3% greater than the fixed mounting arrangement.

articleTitle: Study Results for Preventing Power Outages utilizing Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: As per the favorable Indian and Rajasthan state government policy on renewable energy, the state of Rajasthan is witnessing the large-scale integration of renewable energy. Due to intermittent nature of renewable power, State Load Despatch Centre (SLDC) in Rajasthan is finding difficulty in balancing the power as per scheduled demand & supply scenario. Due to non-availability of spinning and balancing reserve power for the scheduled demand supply adjustment, it results into the over-drawl from the national grid or unanticipated load shedding. This paper explains the present scenario and actions being taken to maintain the demand supply in order to mitigate the intermittent nature of renewable energy. This paper is focusing on feasibility assessment and analysis of utilizing a Renewable Energy Stabilizing System (RESS) and a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) as one of the solutions for balancing of gird power with the report of favorable results obtained from the execution of the research. This paper is based on results obtained from a feasibility study commissioned by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO).

articleTitle: Analysis of distributed energy management scheme for residential consumers using non-cooperative game
abstract: Demand response (DR) technique has resulted in fundamentally shifting the way energy demand is managed in the smart grid. Most of the previous studies focus only on single user energy management. However, it affects the system parameters adversely. Now-a-days, DR schemes focus on finding a solution that works well for individuals as well as overall system behavior. In this paper, a distributed energy management scheme is analyzed to achieve a flat load profile and minimize the energy cost of each user. A real-time price based quadratic cost function is considered to charge the customers. In simulation results, it is shown that the peak as well as the total electricity cost of the system is reduced. Individual energy cost is also minimized.

articleTitle: Development of a Prototype to Study the Effect of Moisture and Temperature on Breakdown Voltage of Transformer Oil
abstract: Aim of this paper is to design and develop a cost effective & user-friendly prototype to study the effect of moisture and temperature on the breakdown voltage of power transformer oil. The designed prototype can be used to maintain the transformer oil at a temperature and moisture. The effects of moisture and temperature on breakdown voltage of the transformer oil also can be studied using this prototype. Firstly, the hardware of the system is designed that is cost effective and gives satisfactory result. Secondly, a program is developed in LabVIEW so that necessary calculations could be done to calibrate sensors & evaluate results received from testing of transformer oil. Efforts are given to make economically as well as technically sound apparatus which is user friendly. It is developed for the purpose of demonstration of the effect of moisture and temperature on breakdown voltage of transformer oil to undergraduate students as well as for research in the High Voltage Engineering Laboratory.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Digital Energy Meters with Power Factor Measurement and Load Indication Feature
abstract: Technology is developing at a fast pace, and so is energy consumption. There is an immediate need for us to transcend from electromechanical meters which measure the energy to digital meters which calibrate it efficiently. The widely used electro mechanical meters are susceptible to changes in temperature and time as a consequence of the mechanical components present in the meter. There are problems associated with the meter reading collection and generation of the bill. The primary objective is to build an energy meter which is able to calibrate the energy accurately, able to determine whether the load is leading or lagging without any human interference and also to make it serve as an communication interface between the consumer and producer. The power factor is measured using XOR logic and the type of load is determined by the microcontroller based on the XOR logic. This helps the consumer gain an insight on what kind of load he/she is consuming, how much reactive power and real power are they paying for and help them control their energy expenses by the real time data analysis. The producers would have a clear idea of demand and supply at instant of time.

articleTitle: Cogent fault diagnosis of photovoltaic-fed single-phase supply system
abstract: The renewable power generation is being extensively used globally so as to overcome the disadvantages of traditional non-renewable sources. The variable power output from the Photovoltaic(PV) is the major concern during its interfacing with the inverter module. This problem can be overcome by connecting quasi-Z source network to obtain constant current fed to the inverter module. This paper presents a study of common occurring switch faults i.e open-circuit and short-circuits faults on the inverter module fed to motor load for the proposed topology. This application is intended for single-phase supply system implemented in the experimental laboratory. The occurrence of faults is an common threat to these facilities and study of effects of faults is necessary in order to design snubber circuits for the power switches. The simulation results of voltage and current waveforms of the proposed system are presented. The effects of faults are investigated by calculating the total harmonic distortion under normal and fault condition.

articleTitle: LMI Based Coordinated Design of PSS and STATCOM Damping Controller For Stability Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a robust coordinated design of power system stabilizer (PSS) and a static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) based damping controller for enhancing power system stability using linear matrix inequality (LMI) approach. A systematic design approach is presented which involves obtaining the power system model using stochastic identification approach. This is followed by development of state feedback controller, and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> state estimator which concurrently estimates the system states obtained from the state feedback controller. Thereafter a coordinated controller is obtained from the feedback controller linking PSS and STATCOM controller to the specific input and output. The coordinated design approach provides enhanced damping characteristics over wide operating conditions in comparison to conventional sequentially designed PSS and STATCOM damping controller. The effectiveness of the proposed coordinated control scheme is tested on IEEE 12 bus benchmark system.

articleTitle: Quantitative analysis of IC Engine waste heat utilization in Biogas Sludge Digester
abstract: Sewage sludge is a source for biogas fuel generation. Biogas production is mainly dependent on maintaining of average temperature of the digester $(36^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ as it influences the ambient temperature which varies drastically from winter to summer in Delhi. In an extreme winter, biogas production would be minimal or stopped. The biogas has higher octane number that can be used in spark ignition engine for electrical power generation and the waste heat coming from the engine can be used to keep the sludge temperature in winter at the desired level. It is observed from this study that the heat requirement of the digester is met by the waste exhaust heat available (engine coolant) in the engine and still surplus heat is available in engine’s exhaust system. The heating load of the digester is higher in winter than summer. The notable conclusion emerged from this study is that the developed methodology can be used for calculating the heat requirement of a sludge digester for maximum yield of biogas as well as finding out potential surplus heat available in a gas engine fueled with biogas.

articleTitle: Implementation of Pre-Filtering Based Adaptive Control for Solar PV System Tied to Weak Grid
abstract: This paper presents a novel pre-filtering based generalized integrator frequency locked loop (PF-GI-FLL) based adaptive control to take care the grid abnormalities during the operation of voltage source converter (VSC) of a grid tied PV generating system (GTPGS). The proposed controller consists of generalized integrator (GI) of second order with a frequency locked loop (FLL). Due of the presence of GI, estimated fundamental components of the current and the voltage, are sensitive to distortion and sub-harmonics. A pre-filtering (PF) based approach is used for eliminating these issues and it has a strong rejection ability of harmonics and improves the response of the system under weak grid conditions as compared to the conventional GI based algorithms. The PF approach provides good isolation from the voltage and current harmonics and FLL is used to estimate the frequency of the signal, which works as feedback for PF to make system adaptive. The proposed PF-GIFLL based control supports the PV array interfaced VSC to satisfy the grid voltage operation under severe grid voltage distortion conditions. The performance of PF-GI-FLL method is demonstrated through experimental results on a developed prototype in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Cascaded Lattice Band Pass Digital Filter Based Control of Three Phase Grid Integrated PV-BES Microgrid
abstract: This paper proposes a single stage solar photovoltaic (PV)-battery energy storage (BES) based microgrid system integrated to the three phase grid. The bidirectional converter incorporates the battery across the DC link of voltage source converter (VSC). The bidirectional controller regulates the discharging and charging current of the battery. The peak power of solar PV array is obtained by perturb and observe (P&O) technique. The sinusoidal fundamental current from the polluted load current, is obtained through a new cascaded lattice band pass digital filter. The control algorithm is utilized for load current harmonics eliminations, power factor correction and load management. The solar PV-BES based microgrid operates in variable climate conditions. The performance and control technique of the proposed system in dynamic and steady state conditions are validated with experimental results on a developed prototype.

articleTitle: Dual Mode Control of Grid Tied Solar PV-DSTATCOM by Utilizing Warped Digital Filter in Distribution System
abstract: For the efficient functioning of grid tied solar photovoltaic array in distribution system, the control algorithm is proposed here utilizing a warped digital filter. The solar photovoltaic (PV) array supplies maximum power to the grid/the load by maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique namely a perturb and observe (P&O) method. The control is termed as a dual mode, as it performs satisfactorily during availability/unavailability of solar PV array power. When the solar PV array power is incident, the proposed system is capable of transferring active power from solar PV array to the grid/the load while improving power quality using a voltage source converter (VSC) working as a distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM). However, during cloudy days or at night, when solar power is not present, the system performs as DSTATCOM for reactive power compensation and elimination of harmonics. The control algorithm provides smooth transition between these modes of operation of the system. The control implemented using warped digital filters, is adaptive as its coefficients are updated depending upon system requirements. A feed-forward term for solar PV array power is incorporated, for the enhancement of dynamic response. A prototype of the system is developed in the laboratory and its performance is studied for varying loads, varying solar insolation conditions and change of modes between grid tied PV array and DSTATCOM.

articleTitle: A new Multi Point Clamped bi-directional DC-DC converter for renewable energy integration
abstract: This paper presents, a multi-point clamped bidirectional DC-DC converter (MPBDC) is presented for targeted applications like multi-level inverter based drive control and integrating renewable energies to two terminal DC grid applications. Multi-level topologies can offer the superior quality of voltage, current profile and minimize the requirement of magnetic components as well as filter size. However, while going higher number of voltage levels with classical multi point clamped multi-level converters (MPC-MLC), the dc link capacitor voltages imbalance takes place when using for active power transfer applications. To address the voltage deviation, an external balancing circuit need to be incorporated. The proposed converter can perform bi-directional DC-DC converter operation along with balance the DC link capacitor's voltage of MPC-MLC. This converter is analysed mathematically and results are verified by MATLAB Simulink model and prototype experimental results.

articleTitle: Improvising Differential Protection Scheme to Differentiate Between Internal and External Fault in Presence of Charging Current
abstract: The paper presents a methodology on how to discriminate: internal and external faults; for a transmission line protected by differential protection scheme, during the presence of charging current. Transmission line with high voltage levels (400-765kV) peculiarly has this disadvantage. Various plots for a Distributed Transmission line Model with Source at both the ends” with internal and external faults were plotted and analyzed. Through the comparison of current samples at zero crossings for remote end and local end buses, after that implementation of proposed DSA (Difference Squared and Averaged) theory, were able to distinguish whether the fault is internal or external. The techniques better compared to conventional techniques since threshold taken under consideration; obtained through experimentation on various system models for varying degree of parameters via certified thresholding method. And the uniqueness lies with the fact that it provides a provision to distinguish transient disturbances from internal fault.

articleTitle: Quadratic Linearization of STATCOM
abstract: Control of STATCOM is important for the stability of power system to which it is connected. Since STATCOM dynamics is nonlinear, various control strategies have been proposed including feedback linearization which involves internal dynamics. In this paper, we propose to quadratic linearize the STATCOM equations and the problem of internal dynamics does not arise in this case. Necessary and sufficient condition for quadratic linearization is derived. An example is given to illustrate the theory.

articleTitle: Synchrophasors Measurement Applications in Controlled Islanding and Restoration
abstract: Controlled islanding has been found as an efficient remedy to stop wide-spread blackouts in power grid under abnormal conditions. Synchrophasor measurements obtained by PMUs are real-time data with high sampling rate of about 48 samples per cycle (50 Hz). It has enhanced the dynamic visualization of the power system status thus fulfilling monitoring requirements of a modern grid. In this work, islanding detection and restoration is examined utilizing PMUs data in Indian power grid. Further, a review on different methodologies used for implementing controlled islanding to prevent blackouts is discussed in the later part.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement By Using DCC-ICC Unipolar CBPWM Based Shunt Active Power Filter
abstract: The aim of this work is modeling of a new topology shunt active power filter (SAPF) using instantaneous reactive power theory (IRPT) technique has been presented. The unipolar carrier based pulse width modulation (UCBPWM) technique using two different current control strategies (i.e. direct and indirect current control techniques) with PI controller has been used for generation of gate pulses for IGBT's connected in voltage source inverter (VSI). The simulation model of three phase three wire power system with three phases shunt active power filter is constructed in MATLAB/SIMULINK and is tested for two different operating conditions (i.e. direct and indirect current control techniques). In this paper, shunt active power filter (SAPF) is constructed using DC storage capacitor and series combination of three phase VSI with three phase parallel RL filter. The parallel RL filter works as a high pass filter (HPF), in which inductor of RL filter works as a delta connected winding of three phase transformer. The simulation result indicates that, the indirect current control (ICC) strategy provides the better performance as compared to direct current control strategy. Since, the indirect current control (ICC) technique gives less harmonic compensation ratio (HCR) as compared to the direct current control (DCC) technique.

articleTitle: Interleaved Landsman Converter Fed EV Battery Charger with Power Factor Correction
abstract: harger followed by a flyback converter, is designed and evaluated to develop a low cost charging solution for the EV battery. A built-in wave-shaping feature is obtained at the front-end of the charger due to power factor correction (PFC) characteristics of the interleaved converter. The converter configuration is developed using two Landsman converter cells, which are designed in DCM mode. The discontinuous conduction mode operation of front-end converter along with the interleaved technology, offers the advantage of zero current switching, reduced sensor used at the output as well as reduced input current and output voltage ripple for battery charger. However, the flyback converter provides the current control during the charging of battery in constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) regions. The proposed charger is evaluated for improved PF based performance under wide input voltage variations. The harmonics spectrum of mains current follows the recommended PQ (Power Quality) regulations such as IEC 61000-3-2 standard.

articleTitle: A Low Ripple Load Regulation Scheme for Grid Connected Microgrid Systems
abstract: The system operating in grid tied mode generally faces a high ripple output problem as the load connected to the grid varies and so the amount of current drawn from the microgrid varies which leads to a mismatch between the actual current and desired current. In this paper, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) is proposed for the co-ordination between the battery side DC-DC converter and grid side Inverter, power quality management of the utility grid. The control method for the DC-DC converter includes a disturbance observer called Luenberger Observer for keep tracking of the DC voltage when subjected to disturbances in DC grid. All the simulation results also presented below and the load regulation is compared with the Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) Output.

articleTitle: High Voltage and its Applications: A Review
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive review on various high voltage generation technique as well as applications of high voltage have been presented. The applications is categorized in various sections like industrial, medical, agriculture etc. The various research areas going on in the field of high voltage engineering world-wide has been presented.

articleTitle: Power Management and Control of PMSG Based Hydro-PV-BES Using CSTOGI Control Algorithm for Autonomous Micro-Grid
abstract: Power management with voltage and frequency control of isolated micro-grid (MG) using permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based hydro –photovoltaic (PV) with a battery energy storage (BES), is dealt in this work. In this system, a bi-directional DC/DC converter (BDC) is used to connect the battery to DC-link of voltage source converter (VSC). The BDC controls the charging and discharging of the battery and provides the DC-link voltage control. The BDC enables to use a BES with reduced rating along with BES is able to manage power flow between hydro and PV array based energy sources. An active power balance is always maintained in the MG between the connected energy sources, thereby maintaining a constant frequency. The VSC along with voltage control also takes care of other power quality problems like reactive power requirement, harmonics and load unbalancing. A combined second and third order generalized integrator (CSTOGI) based control algorithm is proposed for VSC control. In this proposed algorithm, the outputs of third and second-order based generalized integrators (GIs) control structure, are reconstructed and combined together to obtain CSTOGI. It requires tuning of only one damping parameter, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>. This control algorithm has a very simple structure, good dynamic response and good stability.

Author Keywords: Combined third-and second order generalized integrator (CTSOGI)

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of Integrated Renewable Energy System for an un-electrified remote area
abstract: The effective utilization of alternative sources of energy are likely to linked with supply of electrical power to the selected area of consumers in standalone mode. Renewable sources of energy support the high reliability through offering on-site production. Consequently, it results in hybrid scheme that comes under continued existence like SPV panels, micro wind turbine, Biogas energy, Biomass energy, and Small hydro systems. Notably, an integrated renewable energy system (IRES) is highly efficient in relative comparison to grid extension which is far expensive. IRES model is largely based on location and load demand summary where it also considers the accessibility of potential renewable energy sources (RES). This paper demonstrates the modeling and the size optimization of solar, wind, SHP, bio-mass, and bio-gas energy systems for unelectrified remote area in Gujarat. In this sense, seven unelectrified clusters of villages in Limkheda taluka and Dahod district in Gujarat state have been selected as study area. In proposed framework, five renewable energy scenarios are measured. The main objective functions are to find out Total Net Present Cost (TNPC) and Costs of Energy (COE) of proposed structure using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm for every scenario. Estimated energy not fulfilled (EENF) is integrated as a power consistency constraint even as best possible sizing of the structure apparatus.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration of Distribution Network For Power Loss Minimization & Reliability Improvement using Binary Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: This paper describes a method to evaluate optimal configuration of distribution system with minimum active power losses and maximum reliability indices. The optimal configuration is obtained by using Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO). Simple Backward-Forward Load Flow (BFLF) method is applied to calculate active power loss and basic cut-set method is used to evaluate reliability indices. Graph theory-based incidence matrix concept is used during optimization so as to maintain the radial topology of the network and to discard any looped or unconnected configuration. Depth-first Search (DFS) algorithm is utilized to check the connectivity of all nodes and to get intermediate nodes between load point and substation. Detailed study of two distribution networks is done and presented. Various possible configurations are compared based on their power loss and reliability indices. Based on results, recommendation is made for the adoption of network operational topology for desired outcomes.

articleTitle: A Review on Residential Area Demand Response Analysis in Smart Grid Era
abstract: Urbanization of the rural areas increases the residential area load demand of the globe. Again, integration of intermittent renewable energy generations and volatile habits of the domestic users make the household demand profile as unpredictable in nature. Therefore, control of the residential loads is highly required to manage the increasing demand efficiently and also to match the load variability with the available generation to get lowest electricity cost. Advancement in communication technology enables the chance of application of demand response (DR) strategies in the modern smart grid era. DR programs aims to diminish the overall peak consumption of the domestic customers while meeting the power balance constraint at each time interval. This study presents an overview of the articles dealing with the application of demand response analysis in the residential areas.

articleTitle: Role of STATCOM in Mitigating Probabilistic Load Disturbances in Isolated Hybrid Electrical System
abstract: Role of load composition is an important factor for choosing appropriate compensating device from the family of FACTS devices. Devices providing reactive power compensation are important tool for adjusting voltage level in any distributed system. Especially for this paper study, FACTS devices may provide sincere attempts during the abrupt changes in either load or input system conditions such as change in wind speed for wind power generation. From shunt connected FACTS family, STATCOM is a popular voltage source converter (VSC) type compensator that has several merits over reactance based SVC especially for the purpose of voltage control and therefore STATCOM is preferred in many studies in spite of being high compensation tariff compare to that of SVC. In available voltage control studies of Isolated Hybrid System (IHS), STATCOM is applied with deterministic type static load. The accessibility of STATCOM with composite load for mitigating the disturbance, both deterministic and probabilistic, is elaborated in this paper. The effect of static and/ or composite load and deterministic and/or probabilistic load patterns on voltage and reactive power responses in 2.5 MW rating test system of wind diesel based isolated hybrid electrical system is analyzed.

articleTitle: Modelling of Power System Stabilizer for Double Fed Induction Generator based Wind Power System
abstract: This paper presents the Power System Stabilizer (PSS) for the variable speed wind turbine generator of the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG). The mathematical model for DFIG is developed in the synchronous reference by using stator voltage orientation vector control for current and voltage controller and is discretized in time domain. The current controller has two components namely d and q-axis. The d-axis component controls the active power and q-axis component controls the reactive power. The voltage controller converts the dq into ABC-reference frame for rotor and grid side converter. In the proposed control scheme, PSS is designed to improve the performance and efficiency of the system. The proposed two PSSs are (a) Active power stabilizer (b) Reactive power stabilizer. The control strategy with stabilizing parameter of PSS not only improves the dynamic performance but also maintains almost unity power factor to the grid. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by developing the simulation model of 1.5 MW, 575 V, and 50 Hz DFIG based wind turbine in MATLAB/SIMULINK-2013b. In order to explore the robustness of the without and with PSS, simulations are carried out for rapid variation of wind speed and three-phase fault generated in the system. The simulation results show that the proposed PSS have better power control, faster oscillation damping, more accurate regulation, considerably reduced settling time and has fewer ripples in comparison without PSS.

articleTitle: Selection of Input Features for Day-Ahead Electric Load Power Forecasting Based on Artificial Neural Network Technique with Novel Framework in Matlab Environment-A Composite Approach
abstract: In recent years, the electric load power forecasting (ELPF) has become an essential activity in power systems. As per ELPF literatures, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique based models are more accurate than any other. Hence this technique with new framework for day-ahead ELPF which includes features of calendar, weather and lagged load of previous day in time domain is chosen. This research paper is mainly focused to deal with the selection of best suitable weather feature from many weather variables with calendar and lagged load features as constants. The real time data used for this research work were collected from Tata Power Delhi Distribution Utility (TPDDL). The correlation analysis of ELP with respect to each selected feature is performed and presented. Then, suitable framework for development of models is created. The performance criteria for ELPF are chosen and for better understanding, the experimental results are presented with the help of histogram and bar charts. The proposed models produce an average forecast error of 2.6% to 3.3% per hourly samples throughout the year irrespective of seasonal and weather variations. The proposed models are proven for their simplicity, less measurement requirement and easiness in implementation with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Contingency Assessment of Radial Distribution System
abstract: The purpose of the investigation presented in this paper is to obtain the optimal restructure of radial distribution system under the impact of contingencies, with and without the scope of distributed generation. Firstly, solution to occurrence of contingency is proposed by finding out the best switching sequence of a specified number of tie lines and sectionalizes with an objective to improve the continuity of power flow in radial system. Secondly genetic algorithm (GA) has been used to find the optimal location and size of embedded distribution generation (DG), to improve voltage profile and to reduce losses for given load demand. The outcome of the proposed study is illustrated through simulations of loaded 69-bus radial distribution system. The obtained results suggest that the investment is distribution generation is attractive when reconfiguration is used to minimize load curtailment.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Driven Volt/VAr Control for Smart Grid Enabled CVR in Active Distribution Network
abstract: Energy conservation through voltage reduction methodology is becoming popular now a days. Enabling of conservation of voltage reduction (CVR) through smart grid technologies makes informal and effective way. However, the integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) in active distribution grids are facing some operational issues. Moreover, the enabling of CVR through conventional schemes are restricted with limited voltage reduction and unable to cope up during intermittency. This paper proposes a model predictive driven Volt/VAR Control (VVC) scheme for smart grid enabled CVR operation in presence of solar photovoltaic (PV) power system. The impact of uncertainty in PV power generation and error in load forecasting are incorporated in predictive model. Scenario based Volt/VAR optimization (VVO) approach is utilized to CVR deployment. The VVO objective is to minimize the voltage deviations between load node voltage and expected CVR voltage. The VVO problem is solved through particle swarm optimization. In order to avoid the voltage violation due to cloud transients, PV inverter-based VAR has been dispatched as a local voltage control. The proposed CVR method is validated on modified IEEE 13 node feeder of radial distribution network. The simulation results revels that the remarkable energy demand and peak load power is reduced through proposed CVR scheme with suitable feeder voltage profile.

articleTitle: Expert Fuzzy Logic Framework for Remotely Located Solar PV-Wind-BES Microgrid
abstract: This paper proposes an expert speed controller based on Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK)-fuzzy logic controller (FLC) for remotely located solar photovoltaic (PV)-wind-battery energy storage (BES) based microgrid system. The TSKFLC tunes the proportional and integral gains of the proportional integral (PI) controller. The conventional PI controller suffers from the drawbacks of high overshoot and narrow bandwidth during dynamic conditions. These issues are resolved by continuously tuning the controller gains. The TSKFLC adapted PI controller takes the speed error and the change in speed error as input and provides the adjusted gain parameters of the PI controller according to the operating conditions. The reference speed of the wind turbine driven synchronous generator (SG) is obtained using perturb and observe (P&O) maximum power point (MPP) technique, which perturbs the generator speed in the direction of optimal power. The double stage solar PV array with an intermediate boost converter, utilizes an incremental conductance (InC) MPP scheme for maximum power extraction. The flexible power flow is allowed by using a battery at the DC link. A prototype is developed in the laboratory and tested in accordance to IEEE519 standard under steady state and dynamic conditions including variable wind speeds, changing insolation and load removal.

articleTitle: Vulnerability of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IED) to Time Synchronization Spoofing in Power Grid and Jamming of GNSS Receiver
abstract: In recent years the dependency of various electronics devices used in power grids has increased on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), as it is capable to provide real time stamp. Recent investigations have revealed the susceptibility has various application in Marine, farming, military, surveying, science, marine, aviation, power system etc. Intelligent Electronics Devices (IED) such as PMU are highly dependent on time signal obtained from any GNSS. Due to high dependency of IED on GNSS and high vulnerability of GNSS towards time spoofing attacks, the analysis of impact of spoofing attacks has one of the major concern of power grid security. This paper introduces GNSS system, its applications in power system, vulnerability of various IED specially focused on PMU and real time jamming of various GPS/IRNSS/SBAS satellite signals.

articleTitle: A Robust CIM Based Control Approach for PVECS Interfaced To Local Distribution Network
abstract: This paper presents a distribution feeder supported single stage photovoltaic (PV) energy conversion system (PVECS), in which a voltage source converter (VSC) is used. It serves for harnessing maximum power from PV source as well as to inject that harnessed power from PVECS into the distribution feeder with enhanced power quality. The harmonics reduction, distribution feeder currents balancing, power factor correction, compensation of non-sinusoidal load currents are additional attributes provided by proposed single stage. PVECS as compared to traditional PV inverter. The robust correntropy induced metric based normalized least mean fourth algorithm (CIMNLMF) is used here to extract the real power portion of the load currents. Besides, PV contribution is add to distribution feeder currents to improve the dynamic response during varying environmental conditions. The viability of proposed control approach is tested under different ambience conditions through a developed prototype in the laboratory in both conditions either solar power generation available or in absence of it.

articleTitle: A binary differential evolution based memetic algorithm to solve profit based unit commitment problem
abstract: Unit commitment problem (UCP) and profit based unit commitment problem (PBUCP) are two combinatorial optimization problems with several constraints in the power system optimization research. In nowadays, the PBUCP becomes more dominant over the UCP due to restructuring in power industry. In recent years, many researchers have used various evolutionary algorithms to solve the multi-constrained PBUCP but differential evolution (DE) algorithm has received less consideration. A binary differential evolution (BDE) algorithm is introduced in the present research for solving the PBUCP. Further, to enhance the performance of the proposed BDE algorithm, a synergy of the BDE algorithm and a hill climbing local search optimizer (HCLSO) is used to solve the PBUCP. In the proposed synergy, BDE algorithm explores global aspect and a HCLSO method exploits local aspect. A HCLSO is proposed in this paper which makes perturbations in unit status based on a priority of units. A new de-commitment procedure is adopted to de-commit the needlessly committed units. The competency of the proposed BDE algorithm and BDE-HCLSO algorithm has been investigated on 10-units power system for 24 hours scheduling period. Results are justified by performing a comparison with the earlier reported algorithms employed to solve the PBUCP. Further, the simulation results demonstrate that BDE-HCLSO algorithm gives superior results over BDE algorithm.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of the Voltage Pulsations at the Receiver’s Side of a Dynamic Wireless Charging System for Electric Vehicles
abstract: The given study investigates the voltage pulsations at the receiver of the dynamic wireless charging system. Precisely, it was revealed that due to the vehicle's movement, the signal at the receiver's side of the system experience amplitude fluctuations, which may negatively affect the battery of the electric vehicle. An experimental setup consisting of four transmitting coils and one receiving coil is used to imitate the charging scenario and identify the causes of the voltage fluctuations.
